# Introduction

This report analyzes **global seismic activity** during May 2025 using real-time data from the **USGS Earthquake Hazards Program**. The dataset includes **2,022 earthquakes** of magnitude M2.5 and above recorded worldwide between May 1-31, 2025.

**Data source:** [USGS Earthquake Catalog API](https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/feed/v1.0/csv.php)

---

# 1. Data Summary

```{r data-summary}
library(dplyr)

cat(sprintf("**Total earthquakes recorded:** %d (M2.5+)\n", nrow(eq_df)))
cat(sprintf("**Date range:** %s to %s\n", min(eq_df$date), max(eq_df$date)))
cat(sprintf("**Magnitude range:** %.1f to %.1f\n", min(eq_df$magnitude), max(eq_df$magnitude)))
cat(sprintf("**Mean magnitude:** %.2f (SD = %.2f)\n", mean(eq_df$magnitude), sd(eq_df$magnitude)))
cat(sprintf("**Mean depth:** %.1f km\n", mean(eq_df$depth)))
cat(sprintf("**Median magnitude:** %.1f\n", median(eq_df$magnitude)))
cat(sprintf("**Median depth:** %.1f km\n", median(eq_df$depth)))

max_idx <- which.max(eq_df$magnitude)
cat(sprintf("**Strongest earthquake:** M%.1f on %s - %s (depth: %.0f km)\n",
            eq_df$magnitude[max_idx], eq_df$date[max_idx],
            eq_df$place[max_idx], eq_df$depth[max_idx]))
```

```{r class-table, results="asis"}
class_summary <- eq_df %>%
  count(mag_class) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  mutate(pct = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * n / nrow(eq_df)))

knitr::kable(class_summary, caption = "Earthquakes by Magnitude Class", align = "c")
```

# 2. Global Earthquake Map

The map below shows the spatial distribution of all 2,022 earthquakes recorded in May 2025. Size and color encode magnitude class. The **Pacific Ring of Fire** is clearly visible as the dominant seismic zone.

```{r global-map, fig.height=8, fig.width=12}
p1
```

**Key observations from the map:**

* The Pacific Ring of Fire dominates global seismicity, wrapping around the Pacific Ocean
* The Kermadec Islands region (near New Zealand) shows high concentration of moderate-to-strong events
* The Aleutian-Alaska arc (north of the Pacific) is highly active
* Mid-ocean ridges and the Alpine-Himalayan belt also show significant activity
* Most earthquakes occur within the first 100 km of the Earth surface

---

# 3. Magnitude Distribution

```{r mag-distribution, fig.width=10}
p2
```

The magnitude distribution is **right-skewed**, following the well-known Gutenberg-Richter relationship: smaller earthquakes are exponentially more common than larger ones. Approximately **54%** of events fall in the Moderate (M4.0-5.0) range.

---

# 4. Depth vs. Magnitude Analysis

```{r depth-mag, fig.width=10}
p3
```

**Key findings:**

* **75.8% of earthquakes** are shallow (0-70 km depth)
* Intermediate-depth quakes (70-300 km) account for **19.6%**
* Deep earthquakes (300+ km) are rare at **4.6%**
* Stronger earthquakes (M5.0+) tend to occur at greater depths, consistent with subduction zone dynamics
* The log-scale y-axis reveals the full depth range from surface to 700 km

```{r depth-table, results="asis"}
eq_df <- eq_df %>%
  mutate(depth_range = case_when(
    depth < 70 ~ "Shallow (0-70km)",
    depth < 300 ~ "Intermediate (70-300km)",
    TRUE ~ "Deep (300km+)"
  ))

depth_summary <- eq_df %>%
  count(depth_range) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  mutate(pct = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * n / nrow(eq_df)))

knitr::kable(depth_summary, caption = "Earthquakes by Depth Range", align = "c")
```

## 5.2 Magnitude by Date

```{r mag-over-time, fig.width=10}
p6c
```

**Temporal insights:**

* **Average daily activity:** ~65 earthquakes (M2.5+)
* **Peak day:** May 2, 2025 with **99 earthquakes** (driven by the M7.4 Drake Passage event)
* Activity was relatively consistent throughout the month with no obvious clustering pattern beyond the major event on May 2
* The M7.4 Drake Passage earthquake on May 2 was clearly the dominant seismic event of the month

# 7. Strongest Earthquakes (M5.0+)

```{r strong-table, results="asis"}
strong_quakes <- eq_df %>%
  filter(magnitude >= 5.0) %>%
  arrange(desc(magnitude)) %>%
  select(datetime, magnitude, depth, place) %>%
  mutate(date = as.character(format(datetime, format = "%Y-%m-%d")))

knitr::kable(strong_quakes,
             caption = "All earthquakes >= M5.0 in May 2025",
             row.names = FALSE,
             digits = 1)
```

# 8. Key Findings and Conclusions

## Summary Statistics

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Total Earthquakes (M2.5+) | **2,022** |
| Date Range | May 1-31, 2025 |
| Magnitude Range | M2.5 - M7.4 |
| Mean Magnitude | M3.92 (SD = 0.85) |
| Mean Depth | 64.0 km |
| Shallow Events (<70km) | **75.8%** |
| Peak Day | May 2 (99 events) |
| Strongest Event | **M7.4 Drake Passage** |

## Conclusions

1. **Ring of Fire Dominance:** The Pacific Ring of Fire remains the most seismically active region, consistent with global tectonic models.

2. **Magnitude Scaling:** The Gutenberg-Richter relationship is clearly evident - smaller events vastly outnumber larger ones.

3. **Depth Distribution:** Most earthquakes are shallow (<70 km), with deep events concentrated in subduction zones.

4. **M7.4 Drake Passage:** The strongest earthquake of May 2025 occurred on May 2 in the Drake Passage (between South America and Antarctica) at shallow depth (~10 km).

5. **Moderate Activity:** Despite the M7.4 event, the average daily count was ~65 earthquakes, indicating normal global seismic background activity for the month.
